meta.title: Who originally recorded "Piece of My Heart"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not a Janis Joplin original. "Piece of My Heart" was first recorded by Erma Franklin — Aretha's older sister — in 1967 on Shout Records, written by Jerry Ragovoy and Bert Berns. Joplin's 1968 version with Big Brother is a cover.
meta.ogTitle: Who originally recorded 'Piece of My Heart'?
meta.ogDescription: Everyone thinks it's Janis Joplin's song. It's a 1967 soul single by Erma Franklin, Aretha's older sister — written by Jerry Ragovoy and Bert Berns. Joplin's 1968 cover buried the original almost completely.

answer.label: Not a Joplin original — a 1967 Erma Franklin single
answer.sourceLine: This is a cover so overwhelming it erased a real hit: almost everyone takes ‘Piece of My Heart’ for a Janis Joplin original, but Joplin’s 1968 version with Big Brother and the Holding Company is a cover. The song was written by Jerry Ragovoy and Bert Berns and first recorded by Erma Franklin — Aretha’s older sister — in 1967 on Shout Records, where it was a genuine top-10 R&B hit. A year later Joplin’s version buried it almost entirely.

original.charted: Reached No. 10 on the US R&B chart and No. 62 on the Billboard Hot 100; it earned Franklin a Grammy nomination
original.cover: Big Brother and the Holding Company, featuring Janis Joplin — 1968, from the No. 1 album Cheap Thrills on Columbia Records. The single reached No. 12 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became the version the song is now known by; it was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1999.

trail: The song was written by Jerry Ragovoy and Bert Berns and first recorded by Erma Franklin in 1967 for the Shout label Wikipedia ↗.
Franklin’s original was a real hit — a top-10 R&B single that reached No. 62 on the pop chart and drew a Grammy nomination. It was not an obscure B-side; it was a record with its own audience.

The following year Big Brother and the Holding Company, with Janis Joplin on lead vocal, recorded it for the No. 1 album Cheap Thrills. Joplin’s raw rock reading eclipsed the original so completely that Franklin later said she heard it on the radio and did not recognise her own song Erma Franklin ↗.

authors.name: Erma Franklin
authors.heading: About Erma Franklin
authors.bio: Erma Franklin (1938–2002) was an American soul and gospel singer and the older sister of Aretha Franklin. She recorded the first version of ‘Piece of My Heart’ in 1967 — a top-10 R&B hit that earned her a Grammy nomination. Then Janis Joplin covered it, and Erma spent years watching her own recording slip out of public memory; she once said she heard the Joplin version on the radio and did not recognise the song as hers.

authors.name: Janis Joplin
authors.heading: Why it gets pinned on Joplin
authors.metaLine: with Big Brother and the Holding Company · 1968
authors.bio: Janis Joplin sang lead on ‘Piece of My Heart’ with Big Brother and the Holding Company in 1968, on the chart-topping album Cheap Thrills. Her ferocious performance became the definitive one, and the record is usually filed simply under her name — though it was a band recording, and a cover. The song is genuinely hers to sing; the only error is treating a 1968 cover as the place the song began.

authors.name: Jerry Ragovoy & Bert Berns
authors.heading: About the writers
authors.bio: Jerry Ragovoy and Bert Berns wrote ‘Piece of My Heart’ — Ragovoy a soul craftsman behind ‘Time Is on My Side’ and ‘Cry Baby’, Berns the writer-producer behind ‘Twist and Shout’ and ‘Hang On Sloopy’. They are the figures the song’s fame obscures most easily: not the famous performer, not the original singer, but the authors whose composition outlived every act that recorded it.

misattribution.heading: The attribution problem
misattribution.intro: This is a cover-eclipse with a sting in it: nothing about Joplin’s record is wrong or fake, but the original it buried was itself a real hit. The only error is believing the song began in 1968 — a cover mistaken for the source.

items.why: Joplin’s 1968 version with Big Brother and the Holding Company is a cover. The song was recorded a year earlier, in 1967, by Erma Franklin the history ↗.
This was no obscure flop: Franklin’s Shout single was a top-10 R&B hit with a Grammy nomination. That a record this successful could vanish is exactly what makes the eclipse remarkable.
Ragovoy and Berns wrote the song; they are neither the original singer nor the famous one. Performer credit and authorship are different things, and here they belong to different people again.

misattribution.truthLine: Written by Jerry Ragovoy and Bert Berns, first recorded by Erma Franklin in 1967, and made famous — but not originated — by Janis Joplin with Big Brother in 1968 the record ↗.

context.heading: Why the cover ate the original
lead: Most cover-eclipses happen because the original never charted. ‘Piece of My Heart’ is a harder case: Erma Franklin’s 1967 version was a top-10 R&B hit, and it still lost the song. Janis Joplin’s 1968 reading was so much louder, rawer, and better distributed — riding a No. 1 album on a major label — that within a year it simply became the version.

The cruelty of it is in Franklin’s own account: she reportedly heard the cover on the radio and did not recognise the song as hers. She had made a real record, had a real hit, and then watched it be remembered as someone else’s — the original quietly overwritten while she was still around to notice.
detailsBody: Jerry Ragovoy and Bert Berns write ‘Piece of My Heart’.
Erma Franklin records it first, 1967 (Shout) — No. 10 R&B, No. 62 pop, a Grammy nomination.
Big Brother and the Holding Company, with Janis Joplin, cover it in 1968 on Cheap Thrills.
Cheap Thrills hits No. 1; the single reaches No. 12 and becomes the definitive version.
Franklin’s original fades from public memory — later revived when a 1992 UK re-release reached No. 9.
context.pull: She had a real hit, then watched it be remembered as someone else’s.
